ACT_1.secondary: The FBI raided the wrong house in suburban Atlanta — the Supreme Court's own first sentence.
The target: a suspected gang hideout. The warrants named this address.
The house they entered. A quiet family home, three or four houses away.

ACT_1.label: SWAT team members at the door, led by Special Agent Lawrence Guerra

ACT_1.secondary: The team breached the front door and detonated a flash-bang grenade — the Court's account.

lines: BETWEEN THE KNOCK AND THE DOOR.

ACT_1.secondary: Fearing a home invasion, Mr. Cliatt and Ms. Martin hid in a bedroom closet — the Court's account.

ACT_1.quote: Mr. Cliatt took her to the closet because that is where he keeps his shotgun – he planned on defending them against the unknown invaders.
Luckily, the agents opened the closet doors before Mr. Cliatt reached his firearm.

ACT_1.secondary: The family swore an agent held Ms. Martin at gunpoint for about an hour. The court found no agent touched her. The film reports both.

ACT_1.primary: THE BOY IN THE OTHER ROOM
ACT_1.secondary: G.W. pulled the covers over his head — the complaint's words. He is never shown in this film.

ACT_1.quote: G.W. was so afraid that he thought he was going to die.

ACT_1.secondary: Only then did an officer stumble across some mail with the home's address on it — the Court's account.

ACT_1.label: Minutes, at most, that the agents were in the home — a court finding

ACT_1.secondary: The team executed the warrants at the right house — then Agent Guerra returned, and apologized.

ACT_2.secondary: Begun in 2015: an FBI operation concerning violent gang activity in Georgia.

ACT_2.label: Warrants in the Operation Order — seven searches, seventeen arrests

ACT_2.secondary: Agent Guerra says his personal GPS device, set for 3741 Landau Lane, led him to Denville Trace.
The reference point the team navigated by. The suspect was not known to drive one, or to know anyone who did.
The agents noticed neither — the house number was visible on the mailbox at the end of the driveway. A court's description.
A car not present during Agent Guerra's earlier visit sat in the driveway that morning.
Agent Guerra threw the device away not long after the raid — the record's own words.

ACT_2.label: Of sixteen FBI personnel that night, the FBI could find geolocation data for nine — and not for these seven

ACT_2.quote: However, no FBI policy or procedure dictates how to locate or navigate to the target, whether to use a GPS device or what type of GPS device must be used.

lines: NO RULE REQUIRED ANY OF IT.
SO THERE WAS NO RULE TO BREAK.

ACT_2.quote: The Court considers Guerra's overall preplanning to constitute significant 'precautionary measures' to avoid mistake.

ACT_2.secondary: The district court's word for the execution of a search warrant on the wrong family's home.

ACT_3.secondary: Personal injuries and property damage — few explanations and no compensation. The Court's summary.

Times G.W. changed schools due to his emotional state — the complaint's account

ACT_3.secondary: The first paper: detailed tort claims notices to the FBI, one year after the raid.
Suit filed. Martin and G.W. on the 11th; Mr. Cliatt on the 18th; consolidated.
1946: the United States agrees it can be sued like a private person. That is the whole promise.

ACT_3.label: Exceptions that claw the promise back — thirteen ways the sentence ends in “except”

ACT_3.secondary: Assault and false-imprisonment claims survive. Four negligence counts go. Mediation is ordered.
Mediation held. Case did not settle — the docket's five words.
Decided a month after their win, in a different case. The government asks the court to reconsider everything in its light.

ACT_3.quote: The Court acknowledges that the United States could have possibly raised its Supremacy Clause argument earlier.

ACT_3.secondary: Counts I and II dismissed under the Supremacy Clause. The clerk is directed to close the case.
Qualified immunity: the law was not clearly established such that Guerra would have known — the court's finding.
The Eleventh Circuit affirms. Unpublished. Without oral argument.

lines: THEN A CASE THEY WERE NOT PART OF

ACT_4.secondary: Herbert and Evelyn Giglotto woke to the sound of someone smashing down their door — the concurrence's account.

ACT_4.label: State and federal officers who ransacked the Giglottos' home and tied them up at gunpoint

ACT_4.quote: to the sound of someone smashing down their door and bursting into their bedroom
ACT_4.attribution: Martin v. United States (2025) — Sotomayor, J., concurring — the Giglottos' April 1973, in the concurrence's words

ACT_4.primary: THE SECOND HOUSE, THE SAME NIGHT
ACT_4.secondary: The officers moved on to the home of Donald Askew — another innocent couple, another bad tip.
At the Askews' home the officers confessed they had acted on a bad tip — the concurrence's account.

lines: ONE LAW FOR THE WHOLE COUNTRY.

ACT_4.quote: [T]here [was] no effective legal remedy against the Federal Government for the actual physical damage, much less the pain, suffering and humiliation to which the Giglottos and Askews have been subjected.
ACT_4.attribution: Martin v. United States (2025) — Sotomayor, J., concurring, quoting the Senate record

ACT_4.secondary: The law-enforcement proviso: six intentional torts by federal officers may proceed. Written because of Collinsville.

ACT_4.label: Years between Collinsville and Denville Trace — our arithmetic, and a law older than either parent in that house

ACT_4.secondary: Legislative history cannot displace statutory text. Said at full strength, and not rebutted here.

ACT_5.secondary: Certiorari granted, limited to two questions. Neither is whether this family gets a trial.
For the family: Patrick Jaicomo. For the United States: Frederick Liu, Assistant to the Solicitor General.

ACT_5.quote: Oh, he had it identified. He got the right target. He just had the wrong house.
ACT_5.attribution: JUSTICE SOTOMAYOR — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

ACT_5.quote: So I don't understand how the act of going into a wrong house can be discretionary.
ACT_5.attribution: JUSTICE SOTOMAYOR — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

ACT_5.quote: Well, we understand the discretion here to be the discretion as to how to identify the target of a search warrant.
ACT_5.attribution: MR. LIU — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

ACT_5.quote: Yeah, you might look at the address of the house before you knock down the door.
ACT_5.attribution: JUSTICE GORSUCH — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

ACT_5.quote: — number at the end of the driveway means exposing the agents to potential lines of fire from the windows.
ACT_5.attribution: MR. LIU — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

ACT_5.quote: How about making sure you're on the right street?
ACT_5.attribution: JUSTICE GORSUCH — Oral argument transcript, Martin v. United States, 29 April 2025

The Eleventh Circuit hears the case again, on remand. As of this film, it has not ruled.
